name: Mustard Brown
lede: Mustard Brown is a deep, brownish yellow named for prepared mustard, recorded in color charts by the 1920s.

sections.title: From mustard to brown
sections.body:
Paterson defines mustard as a reddish-yellow and mustard brown as a deep brownish-yellow, and adds that a related name, mustard yellow, was popular in the 1930s [1]. Mustard Brown appears in the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930, which gives 1926 as its first recorded use, in the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 (block 58), and in the RAL system [2]. The ISCC-NBS name nearest the swatch is "light olive brown", 4.7 CIEDE2000 units away [2]. The RAL screen value is approximate [2].

Nearby names include [[mustard]], [[mustard-yellow]] and [[ochre]], and the library lists Curry as a near-duplicate, 1.7 units away [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive a color near this one appears in 317 paintings, 1.33% of the total, as photographed [3]. In 72% of the 249 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it plays an accent [3]. It is most devoted to George Dawe, in 7 of his 50 works here, and over-represented in paintings from India, 2.8 times the expected rate [3]. It shares canvases with [[mustard]] and with [[metallic-gold]] [3]. A match shows a screen color near this one in an aged photograph, not a pigment [3].
